report.summary: Change adds shell files (dotfiles) end to end: protocol schemas and limits, D1 table + migration, Worker handlers that write Git objects and push to a per-user Artifacts repo with optimistic CAS on head_sha, a dotfiles.apply op step on create/wake that calls a new tempod request, a read-only egress rule with a WorkspaceDO read token, zsh + Oh My Zsh in the image with defaults mirrored to /etc/tempo/home-defaults, and Settings → Shell on web and Mac. It also reworks terminals into per-terminal tool tabs (web + Mac), moves startup progress into the transcript, and updates spec tabs 01/02/03/04/07/08/09 in the same change. I read every non-eval part of the diff and checked contracts against the generated Artifacts binding types, failure paths (null token -> 403, skip on permanent apply failure with a Setup notice, stale push -> DOTFILES_CHANGED with no D1 change), idempotency of the step and of tempod apply, ownership and reserved-name checks, the container user and file modes, and test structure. No blocking defects found. I could not run typecheck/lint/tests here (running commands needs approval in this session); they rest on CI.

findings.text: The fake Artifacts Git remote accepts a direct POST to git-receive-pack and replies with report-status; nothing in the repo documents that the real Artifacts smart-HTTP service accepts a stateless receive-pack POST without a prior info/refs?service=git-receive-pack advertisement, or replies in this exact format. pushObjects relies on this. Not blocking: a live push in test:conformance or staging would confirm it.

evidence.why: The fake only models the endpoint the writer calls; real-service behavior for an un-advertised receive-pack is unverified in-repo.

findings.text: On the first save, ensureRepository reuses any existing repository named dotfiles-<hash> (ALREADY_EXISTS) without checking it was created by this flow. The Artifacts namespace is shared and, before this change, createRepository/importRepository allowed dotfiles- names, so a legacy repo with that name (requires knowing the victim's userId) would receive the user's files. Not blocking: querying D1 for projects with repo_name LIKE 'dotfiles-%' would show whether any such repo exists.

evidence.why: An existing repository is adopted solely by name match.

findings.text: Every 'ng' push result is reported as DOTFILES_CHANGED, including non-stale rejections and a retried save whose earlier push landed but whose D1 write was lost. Reload recovers both through adoptRemoteTip, as the spec describes, so the only effect is a misleading message.

evidence.why: Any rejection reason maps to the stale-head code.

findings.text: smoke.test.ts was deleted, removing the harness checks that D1 has the app tables and that a CredentialDO round-trips a secret. Other suites probably exercise both. Not blocking.

readSnapshot decodes blobs with a fatal UTF-8 decoder, so a non-UTF-8 blob throws a TypeError that surfaces as INTERNAL instead of ARTIFACTS_API_ERROR. Only Tempo writes the repo (always UTF-8), so this is theoretical.

evidence.quote: const utf8 = new TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true });
evidence.why: The decode error is not mapped to a TempoError.

checked.risk: Real contracts (Artifacts binding, Git smart HTTP/pack format, tempod request schema, Rust generated types)
Failure paths (egress null token, step skip/notice, push rejection, tempod git failures and timeouts)

Idempotency and state (step order on create/wake incl. freshDisk skips, settingsIssues warning add/remove, tempod record/restore, CAS on head_sha, lost D1 write recovery, queue reorder with fixed initial prompt)
Security (ownership by ctx.user.id, owner-only egress config, read-only token scope, reserved dotfiles- repo prefix, path validation, symlink handling, no token in container or logs)
Build and runtime environment (zsh install, Oh My Zsh pinned SHA and read-only, home-defaults copy, login shell, tempod/agents user, versions.json check)
Tests (renamed .cases.ts files still imported, global fetch stub in a sequential group, no sleeps, real git hashes, tempod tests on a real bare remote)

Spec (01 Shell and dotfiles, 02 table/API/error/tempod request, 03 steps and limits, 04/07 Settings → Shell, terminal tabs, startup progress, 09 reserved names and Git transport; web and Mac changed together)
